questions.q: A particle is projected with velocity $u$ so that its horizontal range is three times the maximum height attained by it. The horizontal range of the projectile is given as $\frac{n u^2}{25 g}$, where value of $n$ is : (Given ' $g$ ' is the acceleration due to gravity).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Range }=3 \mathrm{H}_{\max } \\ & \frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin 2 \theta}{\mathrm{~g}}=\frac{3 \mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 \mathrm{~g}}\end{aligned}$
$2 \sin \theta \cos \theta=\frac{3}{2} \sin ^2 \theta$
$\tan \theta=\frac{4}{3} \Rightarrow \theta=53^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$
$\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2\left(2 \times \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{4}{5}\right)}{\mathrm{g}} \Rightarrow \frac{24 \mathrm{u}^2}{25 \mathrm{~g}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:

questions.q: A particle is moving along a circular path with a constant speed of $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. What is the magnitude of the change in velocity of the particle, when it moves through an angle of $60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ around the centre of the circle?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Change in velocity,


|$\Delta \overline{v}|=\sqrt{v_{1}^{2}+v_{2}^{2}+2 v_{1} v_{2} \cos (\pi-\theta)}$

=2 v \sin $\frac{\theta}{2} \quad\left(\because\left|\overrightarrow{v}_{1}\right|=\left|\overrightarrow{v}_{2}\right|\right)=$v

=(2 $\times$10) $\times \sin \left($30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\right)=2 $\times$10 $\times \frac{1}{2}$

=10 m / s

questions.q: Two projectiles are projected at $30 °$ and~$60 °$with the horizontal with the same speed. The ratio of the maximum height attained by the two projectiles respectively is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The maximum height is given by,& $H = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$.

The given data is~

${θ}_{1} = 30 ° {θ}_{2} = 60 ° {u}_{1} = {u}_{2}$

Therefore,

$\dfrac{\left({H}_{1}\right) max}{\left({H}_{2}\right) max} = \dfrac{{u}_{1}^{2}\sin^{2}{θ}_{1}}{{u}_{2}^{2}\sin^{2}{θ}_{2}} = \left(\dfrac{\sin 30 °}{\sin 60 °}\right)2 = \left(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{\dfrac{3}{2}}\right)2 = \dfrac{1}{3}$

questions.q: A man carrying a monkey on his shoulder does cycling smoothly on a circular track of radius $9 \mathrm{~m}$ and completes 120 resolutions in 3 minutes. The magnitude of centripetal acceleration of monkey is \left(\right.$ in $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ) :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given : } \mathrm{R}=9 \mathrm{~m}, \\ & 120 \text { revolution in } 3 \mathrm{~min} \\ & \omega=\frac{120 \mathrm{Rev} .}{3 \mathrm{~min} .}=\frac{120 \times 2 \pi \mathrm{rad}}{3 \times 60 \mathrm\sec}=\frac{4 \pi}{3} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \mathrm{a}_{\text {centripetal }}=\omega^2 \mathrm{R}=\left(\frac{4 \pi}{3}\right)^2 \times 9=16 \pi^2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A boy reaches the airport and finds that the escalator is not working. He walks up the stationary escalator in time ${t}_{1} .$~If he remains stationary on a moving escalator then the escalator takes him up in time ${t}_{2} .$& The time taken by him to walk up on the moving escalator will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$L =$ Length of escalator

${V}_{b / ecc} = \dfrac{L}{t1}$

When only escalator is moving,~

${V}_{esc} = \dfrac{L}{t2}$

when both are moving,~

${V}_{b / g} = {V}_{b / esc} + {V}_{esc}$

${V}_{b / g} = \dfrac{L}{t1} + \dfrac{L}{t2} ⇒ \left[$t = \dfrac{L}{Vb / g} = \dfrac{{t}_{1}{t}_{2}}{{t}_{1} + {t}_{2}}\right]$

$

questions.solution:
The instantaneous acceleration of tip is given by

questions.q: Two projectiles are fired from ground with same initial speeds from same point at angles  \left(45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}+\alpha\right)$ and  \left(45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}-\alpha\right)$ with horizontal direction. The ratio of their times of flights is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\theta_1=45+\alpha ; \theta_2=45-\alpha$
Time of flight, $\mathrm{T}=\frac{2 \mathrm{v} \sin \theta}{\mathrm{g}}$
$\frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{\sin (45+\alpha)}{\sin (45-\alpha)}$
$\frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \alpha+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin \alpha}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \alpha-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin \alpha}$
$\frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{\cos \alpha+\sin \alpha}{\cos \alpha-\sin \alpha}=\frac{1+\tan \alpha}{1-\tan \alpha}$

questions.q: A stone of mass $1$ kg is tied to end of a massless string of length $1m$. If the breaking tension of the string is $400N$, then maximum linear velocity, the stone can have without breaking the string, while rotating in horizontal plane, is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In horizontal circle, tension towards the centre of the circular path at any moment will provide the required centripetal force.

Therefore,

${T}_\max = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} ⇒ 400 = \dfrac{1 \times v^{2}}{1} ⇒ v = 20ms^{- 1}$

$\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}=5 t^2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-5 \mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{j}} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=10 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{j}} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=20 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{j}} \quad \text { at } \mathrm{t}=2 \mathrm\sec\end{aligned}$

A plane is inclined at an angle $\alpha = 30 °$ with respect to the horizontal. A particle is projected with a speed $u = 2ms^{- 1}$ , from the base of the plane, making an angle $\theta = 15 °$ with respect to the plane as shown in the figure. The distance from the base, at which the particle hits the plane is close to:
(Take $g = 10ms^{- 2}$ )

questions.solution:
Range $= \dfrac{2u^{2}sin\alpha cos \left(\alpha + \theta\right)}{g\cos^{2} \theta}$
$\alpha = angleofinclination = 30 °$
$\theta = angleofprojectionfrominclination = 15 °$
$u = 2m / s$
$R = \dfrac{2{\left(2\right)}^{2}\sin 15 ° \cos \left(15 ° + 30 °\right)}{g\cos^{2} 30 °} = \dfrac{8\sin 15 °\cos 45 °}{gcos^{2}30 °} \left[$\sin 15 ° = $\dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{2\sqrt{2}}\right]
$R = $\dfrac{4}{5}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{3}\right) \approx$0.2m$
$R $\approx$20$ cm$

questions.q:
A boy ties a stone of mass $100g$ to the end of a $2m$ long string and whirls it around in a horizontal plane. The string can withstand the maximum tension of $80N$. If the maximum speed with which the stone can revolve is $\dfrac{K}{π}rev\min^{- 1}$. The value of $K$ is :
(Assume the string is massless and un-stretchable)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The maximum angular velocity of the stone is& $\omega = rpm \times \dfrac{2\pi}{60} = \dfrac{K}{30}rads^{- 1}$

The tension in the string will provide the required centripetal force. Therefore,

$T = m{ω}^{2}l ⇒ 80 = 0 . 1 \times \left(\dfrac{K}{30}\right)2 \times 2 ⇒ K^{2} = 360000 ⇒ K = 600$

questions.q: Projectiles $A$ and $B$ are thrown at angles of $45 °$ and $60 °$ with vertical respectively from top of a $400m$ high tower. If their times of flight are same, the ratio of their speeds of projection ${v}_{A}: {v}_{B}$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For same time of flight, vertical component of velocity of projection must be same. Therefore,

${v}_{A}\sin 45 ° = {v}_{B}\sin 30 ° ⇒ \dfrac{vA}{vB} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}} ⇒ \dfrac{vA}{vB} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q: A vehicle of mass $200$ kg is moving along a levelled curved road of radius $70m$ with angular velocity of $0 . 2rads^{- 1}$. The centripetal force acting on the vehicle is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The centripetal force is given by&

$F = \dfrac{Mv^{2}}{R} = MR{ω}^{2}$

The given data is~

$M = 200kgR = 70m\omega = 0 . 2rads^{- 1}$

The magnitude of the force is~

$F = 200 \times 70 \times 0 . {2}^{2}N$

$⇒ F = 560N$

questions.q: A ball is projected with kinetic energy $E$, at an angle of $60 °$ to the horizontal. The kinetic energy of this ball at the highest point of its flight will become :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$E = \dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2}$

At the Highest point, velocity is equal to the horizontal component of the velocity of projection. Therefore,

$v = ucos60 ° = \dfrac{u}{2}$

$∴$ Kinetic energy~at the~topmost point $= \dfrac{1}{2}m\left(\dfrac{u}{2}\right)2 = \dfrac{E}{4}$

questions.q: A ball is spun with angular acceleration $\alpha = 6t^{2} - 2t$ where $t$ is in second and $\alpha$ is in~$rads^{- 2}$. At $t = 0$, the ball has angular velocity of $10rads^{- 1}$ and angular position of $4rad$. The most appropriate expression for the angular position of the ball is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:& $\alpha = 6t^{2} - 2t$

Using relation~$\alpha = \dfrac{d \omega}{d t} = 6t^{2} - 2t$

Integrating the above,~

${∫}_{10}^{ω} d \omega = {∫}_{0}^{t}\left(6t^{2} - 2t\right) d t$

$⇒ \omega - 10 = 2t^{3} - t^{2}$

Now,~$\omega = \dfrac{d \theta}{d t} = 10 + 2t^{3} - t^{2}$

${∫}_{4}^{θ} d \theta = {∫}_{0}^{t}\left(10 + 2t^{3} - t^{2}\right) d t$

Integrating the above relation,~

$\theta - 4 = 10t + \dfrac{t4}{2} - \dfrac{t3}{3}$

Thus, angular position of the ball is~$\theta = \dfrac{t4}{2} - \dfrac{t3}{3} + 10t + 4$.

questions.q: A body of mass $M$ thrown horizontally with velocity $v$ from the top of the tower of height $H$ touches the ground at a distance of $100 \mathrm{~m}$ from the foot of the tower. A body of mass $2 \mathrm{M}$ thrown at a velocity $\frac{v}{2}$ from the top of the tower of height $4 \mathrm{H}$ will touch the ground at a distance of _____{\mathrm{m}}.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 100=v \sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{g}}} ; \quad \mathrm{x}=\frac{v}{2} \sqrt{\frac{2(4 \mathrm{H})}{\mathrm{g}}}=v \sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{g}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=100\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The speed of a swimmer is $4kmh^{- 1}$ in still water. If the swimmer makes his strokes normal to the flow of river of width $1$ km, he reaches a point $750m$ down the stream on the opposite bank. The speed of the river water is ______~$kmh^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let& ${v}_{r}$~be velocity of river and~${v}_{m}$~be velocity of man.

Time taken by man to cross the river of width~$= 1000m$~is~$t = \dfrac{1}{4}h$.

Now, drift $x = {v}_{r} \times t$

$⇒ 0 . 750 = {v}_{r} \times \dfrac{1}{4} ⇒ {v}_{r} = 3kmh^{- 1}$

questions.q: A car is moving on a circular path of radius $600m$~such that the magnitudes of the tangential acceleration and centripetal acceleration are equal. The time taken by the car to complete first quarter of revolution, if it is moving with an initial speed of $54kmh^{- 1}$ is $t ( 1 – e^{– \dfrac{π}{2}} ) s$. The value of $t$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

Initial speed& $= \dfrac{54 \times 1000}{3600} = 15ms^{- 1}$

\left|{a}_{t}\right| = \left|{a}_{c}\right|$

$⇒ v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{v2}{R} ⇒ {∫}_{15}^{v}\dfrac{dv}{v} = \dfrac{1}{R}{∫}_{0}^{x}dx$

$⇒ v = 15e\dfrac{x}{R}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dt} = 15e\dfrac{x}{R}$

Distance covered in first quarter of revolution~$= \dfrac{2\piR}{4} = \dfrac{\piR}{2}$.

Therefore,

${∫}_{0}^{\piR2}e^{- \dfrac{x}{R}}dx = 15{∫}_{0}^{t0}dt$

$⇒ {t}_{0} = 40 \left(1 - e^{- \dfrac{π}{2}}$\right)$

Hence,~$t = 40$.

$

questions.q: A body is projected from the ground at an angle of $45 °$ with the horizontal. Its velocity after $2s$ is $20\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. The maximum height reached by the body during its motion is _____~$m$. (use $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
After& $2s$~the velocity is~$20ms^{- 1}$

$⇒ {v}_x^{2} + {v}_y^{2} = v^{2} = 400$

$⇒ u^{2}\cos^{2}45 ° + \left(usin45 ° - gt\right)2 = \dfrac{u2}{2} + \left(\dfrac{u}{2} - 20\right)2 = 400$

$⇒ \dfrac{u2}{2} + \dfrac{u2}{2} + 400 - \dfrac{40}{2}u = 400$

~$⇒ u^{2} = \dfrac{40}{2}u ⇒ u = \dfrac{40}{2}ms^{- 1}$

Now the maximum height of the projectile is given by,

$H = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g} ⇒ H = \dfrac{1600}{20 \times 2 \times 2} = 20m$
